title: Impact of Stock Split Announcements on Cumulative Abnormal Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology. This approach measures the abnormal returns around the stock split announcement by comparing actual returns to expected returns based on a market model. The key assumption is that the market model accurately captures normal returns in the absence of the event, and that the announcement represents an exogenous shock that allows us to isolate the market's reaction to the stock split news.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s55_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns using market model
# AR = actual return - (alpha + beta * market return)
# For simplicity, assume alpha = 0 (common in event studies)
data$abnormal_return <- data$ret - (data$beta * data$mkt_ret)

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for different windows
# Event window: -2 to +2 days around announcement (day 0)
event_window <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -2 & event_day <= 2) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_event = sum(abnormal_return, na.rm = TRUE))

# Pre-event window: -10 to -3 days (placebo test)
pre_event <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -3) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_pre = sum(abnormal_return, na.rm = TRUE))

# Post-event window: +3 to +10 days
post_event <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= 3 & event_day <= 10) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_post = sum(abnormal_return, na.rm = TRUE))

# Combine all CARs
car_results <- merge(event_window, pre_event, by = "stock_id", all = TRUE)
car_results <- merge(car_results, post_event, by = "stock_id", all = TRUE)

# Main results: Test significance of event window CAR
cat("=== MAIN RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Event Window CAR (-2 to +2 days):\n")
t_test_event <- t.test(car_results$CAR_event)
cat("Mean CAR:", round(mean(car_results$CAR_event, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
cat("T-statistic:", round(t_test_event$statistic, 3), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(t_test_event$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(t_test_event$conf.int[1], 4), ",", round(t_test_event$conf.int[2], 4), "]\n")

# Calculate daily average abnormal returns
daily_ar <- data %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_ar = mean(abnormal_return, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_ar = sd(abnormal_return, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    t_stat = mean_ar / se_ar,
    p_value = 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat), n() - 1))
  ) %>%
  arrange(event_day)

cat("\n=== DAILY ABNORMAL RETURNS ===\n")
print(daily_ar[daily_ar$event_day >= -2 & daily_ar$event_day <= 2, ])

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Pre-event CAR (should be close to zero)
t_test_pre <- t.test(car_results$CAR_pre)
cat("Pre-event CAR (-10 to -3):\n")
cat("Mean:", round(mean(car_results$CAR_pre, na.rm = TRUE), 4), 
    "| P-value:", round(t_test_pre$p.value, 4), "\n")

# 2. Post-event CAR
t_test_post <- t.test(car_results$CAR_post)
cat("Post-event CAR (+3 to +10):\n")
cat("Mean:", round(mean(car_results$CAR_post, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    "| P-value:", round(t_test_post$p.value, 4), "\n")

# 3. Alternative event windows
car_narrow <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_narrow = sum(abnormal_return, na.rm = TRUE))

car_wide <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -5 & event_day <= 5) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_wide = sum(abnormal_return, na.rm = TRUE))

t_test_narrow <- t.test(car_narrow$CAR_narrow)
t_test_wide <- t.test(car_wide$CAR_wide)

cat("CAR (-1,+1):", round(mean(car_narrow$CAR_narrow, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    "| P-value:", round(t_test_narrow$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("CAR (-5,+5):", round(mean(car_wide$CAR_wide, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    "| P-value:", round(t_test_wide$p.value, 4), "\n")

# Summary statistics
cat("\n=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===\n")
cat("Number of firms:", nrow(car_results), "\n")
cat("Percentage of positive CARs:", 
    round(100 * sum(car_results$CAR_event > 0, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(car_results), 1), "%\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive and statistically significant CAR of approximately 1-3% in the event window around stock split announcements. Stock splits are generally viewed as positive signals by the market, indicating management's confidence in future performance and making shares more accessible to retail investors. The reaction should be strongest on the announcement day (day 0) and the day after, with some anticipation effects possibly visible in the day before. The pre-event window should show insignificant abnormal returns (validating our methodology), while post-event returns may show some continuation or reversal depending on whether the initial reaction was appropriate.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare CAR before and after the stock split announcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The announcement of a stock split is associated with a decrease in CAR.
